title: GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2608.25583v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reasoning-oriented large language models often achieve strong problem-solving performance by generating long chains of thought, but this behavior substantially increases inference cost and latency. In contrast, instruction-tuned models tend to answer more concisely, yet often lack comparable reasoning ability. This accuracy-efficiency mismatch motivates a lightweight approach that combines the strengths of both models without full model retraining. In this paper, we propose GRIP (Granular Reward-guided Interpolation of Parameters), a reward-guided parameter interpolation framework for efficient reasoning. Given a reasoning model and an instruction model with identical architectures, GRIP assigns learnable interpolation ratios to individual modules and optimizes only these ratios while keeping both source models frozen. The interpolation ratios are trained with a reward signal that favors responses that are both correct and concise. Exper

translated_title: GRIP：基于粒度奖励引导的参数插值方法用于高效推理
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.25583v1 公告类型：新论文  摘要：面向推理的大型语言模型通常通过生成较长的思维链来实现强大的问题解决性能，但这种行为会显著增加推理成本和延迟。相比之下，指令微调模型往往回答得更简洁，但通常缺乏相当的推理能力。这种准确性与效率之间的不匹配促使我们提出一种轻量级方法，在不进行完整模型重训练的情况下，结合两种模型的优势。在本文中，我们提出了GRIP（粒度奖励引导的参数插值），一种用于高效推理的奖励引导参数插值框架。给定一个推理模型和一个具有相同架构的指令模型，GRIP为各个模块分配可学习的插值比例，并在保持两个源模型冻结的同时仅优化这些比例。插值比例通过一个奖励信号进行训练，该信号偏好既正确又简洁的回答。实验...
tldr: 本文提出GRIP框架，通过仅优化推理模型与指令模型之间的模块级参数插值比例，在保持推理能力的同时提升响应简洁性，从而在不重训练的情况下实现高效推理。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes GRIP, a framework that optimizes only module-level parameter interpolation ratios between a reasoning model and an instruction model, balancing reasoning ability and response conciseness for efficient inference without full retraining.
